main_text.p: dendo, aut occidendo, in jura Dei, & magistratuum, involant. Resp. 3. Nec amittitur fama apud homines sapientiores, sed conservatur, si quis suis affectibus, modū ac mensuram posuerit. Nam si rem æquâ lance ponderemus, deprehendemus potius nos nobismet aliquam maculam inurere in certamen descendendo. Aut enim (loquar secundum illud Diogenis ad Ciernum[?] è victoriâ Pancratii redeuntem) cum tali tibi negotium, qui te valore ac robore inferior; quem si feRIeris, ignominia in te redundabit, quod in imparem insurrexeris. Aut contendis cum fortiore cui impar es, à quo si fueris superatus, notaberis aliquâ facti infamiâ, quasi tibi defuisset animus. page.notes: Ciernum[?]: doubtful reading, probably a proper name (Cleanthes, Diogenes' correspondent). "feRIeris" is printed as "fe-rieris" with the hyphen at the line end; the text is copied as printed. A blot sits over the word "inferior" and the line below it; it is a stain, not text. "suc-" at the line end is hyphenated and continues into the catchword "cum". The printed "valore" and "Resp. 3." are copied as printed.
